system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one into the fixed
template below so that a reader cannot tell what field, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, nor what
kind of work it is: an experiment, a new procedure, a measurement suite, a write-up choice, or a decision about what
to share or fund must all read alike. Keep the trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

Template, one entry per item:
- "situation": one sentence, at most 30 words: the position the researcher was in when the decision came up.
- "options_considered": two or three short options separated by " / ", including the one taken. If the source names
  no alternative, give the plain opposite of what was done.
- "choice": one sentence, at most 25 words, starting with "Chose", saying which option was taken.
- "reason": one sentence, at most 25 words, giving the stated reason; if none is stated write "No reason stated."

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, procedures, organisations, people,
  papers and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area.
- Use only plain generic words such as: the result, the claim, the finding, the check, the comparison, the setup,
  the change, the next step, the question, the work, the variant, the condition, the sample, the system.
- Never use any of these words or any form of them: ability, access, accuracy, allow, appeared, assessment, attack, avoid, baselines, behavior, behaviour, benchmark, best, bound, call, capability, cheap, claiming, clean, comes, complex, components, content, cost, defense, difficulty, disclosure, effect, effects, error, evaluate, evaluated, evaluating, evaluation, evaluator, evaluators, failures, features, form, format, four, gains, generalise, generalization, generalize, ground, harm, harmful, implication, improve, improvement, information, internal, intervention, judged, key, limit, matched, mechanism, method, methods, metric, observed, organisation, pattern, performance, phenomenon, picture, point, policy, possibly, practical, preference, preferences, public, publication, publish, rater, reduce, release, residual, responses, risk, rule, safety, sampled, say, score, shifts, similar, source, stage, success, supporting, task, tasks, technique, time, tool, tools, trait, transfer, transferred, treatment, unintended, unmodified, unwanted, value, varies, verify, wording.
- Add nothing that is not in the source. Never say who made the decision. Write every item in the same plain style.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "situation": ..., "options_considered": ..., "choice": ..., "reason": ...}, ...]}
with one entry per input item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:572c442292c0",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim IP's general effectiveness given mixed results on compliance with explicit harmful requests.",
  "did": "They reported in the limitations that IP increased tendency to follow undesired instructions in two of six models and that it may make the model easier to misuse, rather than claiming uniform safety.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "In two out of six models tested, IP increased the tendency to follow instructions requesting the undesired behavior (e.g. Qwen 2.5 base)."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:1be7b75f55b5",
  "problem": "Whether to continue analyzing the defense after it was modified again by the authors after the first release.",
  "did": "Continued the work: attacked the third code release using the authors' pretrained CIFAR-10 model and updated the paper, as promised in the original disclaimer.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The first version promised to analyze future modifications once the authors provided a pretrained model."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:24b5ec49b091",
  "problem": "Whether baseliners should be allowed internet access when some tasks could be trivialized by external resources.",
  "did": "They always permitted web access to baseliners but banned AI assistants, Wolfram Alpha, and sign-in services.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "restricting internet access for baseliners"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Pilot studies showed significantly reduced human performance without web access, often from small hindrances like forgetting syntax."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:a820806bfca9",
  "problem": "Whether to continue investing in optimizing the baseline detection methods or to keep them as unoptimized baselines.",
  "did": "They left the detection methods unoptimized and did not try to fix all identified problems.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "optimizing the detection methods to maximize detector performance"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The goal was to provide an evaluation testbed rather than to maximize detector performance."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:816e585bbdc1",
  "problem": "Which attack scenarios to implement as proofs-of-concept versus leave as speculation.",
  "did": "They implemented realistic ethical proofs-of-concept in Section 3 and relegated attacks lacking a realistic, ethical test method to Section 4 as unvalidated discussion.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "implementing every attack vector"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "They could not easily identify a method for a realistic and ethical proof-of-concept for those attacks."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:faf4a2f358d2",
  "problem": "Whether IP makes models more likely to produce unwanted or harmful outputs when explicitly requested, a possible side effect of training with such instructions.",
  "did": "They evaluated IP-trained models using the inoculation prompt as the evaluation prompt and also ran Strong Reject for broader harmful compliance.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To test whether IP increases compliance with unwanted requests compared to models trained without IP."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:b9e670003010",
  "problem": "How to evaluate whether elicitation techniques actually reveal secrets rather than just producing noise or misleading the auditor.",
  "did": "Ran a control condition extracting the same white-box information from the untuned base model and compared it to the secret-keeping model.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To confirm the signal is specific to the fine-tuned secret-keeping model rather than an artifact of the extraction method."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:80462528f506",
  "problem": "Whether to include a Hitler-persona inoculation seed that failed to suppress the persona",
  "did": "Excluded the single failed seed from the analysis.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "include all 10 seeds"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Inoculation did not suppress the persona without a system prompt in that seed, so the seed was excluded."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:9ab3c6acd1cc",
  "problem": "Which kinds of tasks should be collected first to measure autonomous agent capability across a useful range of difficulty.",
  "did": "They chose to prioritize collecting harder tasks first, planning to derive easier variants from them by adding guidance or reducing requirements.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "collecting easier tasks first",
   "shorter tasks"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Easier variants of hard tasks can be made fairly straightforwardly, whereas hard tasks are the scarce, more informative resource."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:0706849ae382",
  "problem": "Whether to build tasks around specific threat models or around general capabilities.",
  "did": "They focus on general capabilities, treating specific threat-model information as a bonus.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "ruling out specific threat stories"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "It seems hard to rule out danger from a broadly capable agent just by ruling out specific threat stories."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:4b4120251254",
  "problem": "How to choose the target-model layer to read from and the decoder layer to write to without an a priori basis.",
  "did": "They ran a hyperparameter sweep over read and write layers, scoring each by lowest test loss on a held-out evaluation set, and used the best configuration for all experiments.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The k=15, l=0 configuration had the best generalization on the evaluation dataset."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:e97115918b83",
  "problem": "How to detect conditional misalignment when the triggers are unknown",
  "did": "Named two options: expanding default evaluations as much as possible, or using tools like SURF. Did not commit to either.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "expand default evaluations",
   "SURF"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Practitioners are unlikely to guess the cues, and exhaustively searching the trigger space may not be practical."
 }
]
